QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_5

question.text: Mr. Arjun Mehra, a first-time LP, is evaluating three investment routes: (i) a Category I VC Fund, (ii) a Category I Angel Fund, and (iii) a Category II Private Debt Fund. All three are ordinary (non-LVF, non-Accredited-Investor) schemes. According to the SEBI (AIF) Regulations as described in Chapter 3, what is the minimum investor commitment per investor for the Category I VC Fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF comparison in Chapter 3, investors in a standard Category I AIF (including a VCF) must invest a minimum of INR 1 crore. This floor is not applicable to Angel Funds (where no minimum value applies for investment in an Angel Fund by an angel investor) and is replaced by a higher INR 25 crore threshold for Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors. The Trap: INR 10 lakh is the lower end of the Angel Fund per-investee-company investment range (INR 10 lakh to INR 25 crore), not an investor-level minimum for a VCF. INR 25 lakh is the employee/director carve-out under the general AIF regime, not the Angel Fund or VCF investor minimum. INR 5 crore is not the source-backed LVF figure — the LVF investor minimum is INR 25 crore. Note: Angel Fund investor minimum and Angel Fund per-investee investment are different concepts in the source; do not conflate them with the Cat I/II INR 1 crore investor floor.
